commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Say where to run the relaunch command
commitResults.messageBody:
The Help-and-exit steps tell the tester to relaunch with
`java -jar larperboard.jar` but not where. Run from any other folder,
the command fails with "Unable to access jarfile".

Let's,
* say to `cd` to the folder that contains the JAR before the first
  relaunch
* refer to that way of relaunching in the second one

Testers can then copy the steps and get the behaviour described.

commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Tell testers to edit, not add, data fields
commitResults.messageBody:
The malformed-data tests say to add `"followUpDate"` or `"createdAt"`
to a contact. A file saved by the app already has both fields as
`null`. A tester who adds the new line above the old one has it
silently overridden, so the app starts normally instead of with an
empty list, and the Expected line is wrong. After a failed start, any
command also saves an empty list over the file.

Let's,
* say that saved files already list every field and that a repeated
  name is won by the later line
* word the cases as changing the existing value
* say to restore the backup between cases after running a command

This makes each test case give the result it states.
Correct follow-up and relaunch manual tests in DG

commitResults.messageTitle: Acknowledgements: Credit AB3, libraries and AI use
commitResults.messageBody:
The Developer Guide acknowledgements section was still the AB3
placeholder, and the README only listed libraries. The course requires
reused material and the use of AI tools to be acknowledged in the
Developer Guide.

List AB3 and the SE-EDU material we build on, the third-party libraries
and build tools, and how AI tools were used. Add a short pointer to
that section in the README.
Credit AB3, libraries and AI use in acknowledgements

commitResults.messageTitle: Find: Hint that plain find searches names only
commitResults.messageBody:
A plain find such as find devops only looks at names, but a search
with no matches only said 0 contact(s) listed!. A tester looking for a
tag spent a long time before finding out that tags need find t/TAG.

Add a second line to the result of a plain find that lists nothing,
saying that it searches names only and how to search tags. Typed finds
and finds with matches keep their messages. Test the three cases and
describe the line in the User Guide and Developer Guide.

Fixes #278

commitResults.messageTitle: Find: Reword the hint for a find without prefix
commitResults.messageBody:
The hint on a find that lists nothing said "Plain find", a term only
the User Guide uses, and only pointed to tag search. A user who
searches for a note or an event name hits the same wall.

Say that a find without a prefix searches names only, and show how to
search tags, notes and events. Update the User Guide, the Developer
Guide and the tests to match.
Hint that plain find searches names only

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep card tag row stable on selection
commitResults.messageBody:
The contact card gets its 1px border only when selected. Selecting
or deselecting a card changes the space inside it, so the tag row
refits: chips can appear or vanish, and the +N overflow count
changes with focus alone (#275).

Give every card a transparent 1px border and change only its color
on selection. The card's layout is the same in both states, so the
visible chips and +N depend only on the list width.

Add a JavaFX regression test that sweeps the list width and toggles
selection and focus. It checks that the shown tags, the overflow
count and the unclipped chips stay the same. Add manual-testing
steps and record the AI tool use in the Developer Guide.
Keep card tag row stable on selection
